items.title: Continuous symmetries of the model's mechanical Lagrangian: symmetry data, the Noether identity, the charge and its dimensions
items.statement:
Adopt one force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ particle
labels with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ (clause (i)), an open
nondegenerate time window $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration
domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and a force map $F$ with the standing
continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause (iii) of that
postulate, and fix one inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]). Adopt in addition a potential presentation
$(U,d)$ of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]: a function
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ with $F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$,
with residual forces $d=(d_{1},\dots,d_{N})$ of the standing regularity. Let
$L=K-U$, $O:=I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and $\mathsf M$ be the
mechanical Lagrangian, the chart domain and the mass operator of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], so that $L$ is of class $C^{2}$
on the open set $O$; when $Q\ne\varnothing$, $(O,L)$ is a time-dependent
Lagrangian chart over every $[a,b]\times Q$ with $a<b$ and
$[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$
([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], inner products and norms are Euclidean
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. For a $C^{1}$ function
$\varphi$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and
$(t,x,v)\in O$ write

$$D_{t}\varphi(t,x,v):=\varphi_{t}(t,x)+\varphi_{x}(t,x)\cdot v,$$

the derivative of $s\mapsto\varphi(s,x+v(s-t))$ at $s=t$; the last two slots
of $L$ are $(x,v)$, and $L_{t}$, $L_{x}$, $L_{v}$ are the gradients of $L$ in
its three slots ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

**(a) Symmetry datum.** A **symmetry datum of the model's mechanical
Lagrangian** is a triple $(\tau,\xi,B)$ of maps

$$\tau:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R,\qquad \xi:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad B:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R,$$

of class $C^{2}$, that satisfies for every $(t,x,v)\in O$ the **Noether
identity of the model**:

$$L_{t}(t,x,v)\,\tau(t,x)+L_{x}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(t,x)+L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot\bigl(D_{t}\xi(t,x,v)-v\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)\bigr)+L(t,x,v)\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)=D_{t}B(t,x,v).$$

Because $K(v)=\tfrac12 v\cdot\mathsf M v$ does not depend on $t$ or $x$ and
$U$ does not depend on $v$, the identity is the following identity among the
model's data:

$$-U_{t}(t,x)\tau(t,x)-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\cdot\xi(t,x)+\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\bigl(D_{t}\xi(t,x,v)-v\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)\bigr)+\bigl(K(v)-U(t,x)\bigr)D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)=D_{t}B(t,x,v).$$

It involves the declared potential $U$, the masses through $\mathsf M$, and
the boundary function $B$; it is an identity imposed on the model's declared
data on the whole state domain $O$.

**(b) Strict data and point symmetries.** A symmetry datum is **strict**
when $\tau\equiv0$; its identity reads
$L_{x}\cdot\xi+L_{v}\cdot D_{t}\xi=D_{t}B$. The following chart
identification is for $Q\ne\varnothing$. If a strict datum has $\xi$
independent of $t$, then the pair $(\xi,B)$ is an **infinitesimal point
symmetry of the chart $(O,L)$** in the sense of
[[def-cm-infinitesimal-point-symmetry]]: that definition's identity,
instantiated with $n=3N$ in the configuration slot, is verbatim
$L_{x}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(x)+L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot D\xi(x)v=B_{t}(t,x)+B_{x}(t,x)\cdot v$.
Conversely every infinitesimal point symmetry of the chart $(O,L)$ whose
generator and boundary function are of class $C^{2}$, with the boundary
function defined on $I_{0}\times Q$, is a strict datum with $\xi$ independent
of $t$. A general datum is a **point symmetry with time
reparametrisation**: the family

$$x_{i}\longmapsto x_{i}+s\,\xi_{i}(t,x),\qquad t\longmapsto t+s\,\tau(t,x)$$

changes the coordinate velocity to first order by $D_{t}\xi-v\,D_{t}\tau$, and
the identity says that the infinitesimal variation of $L$ along the family is
the total time derivative $D_{t}B$ of the chart function $B$.

**(c) Charge.** The **charge of the datum** is the function

$$C:O\to\mathbb R,\qquad C(t,x,v):=L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(t,x)-E(t,x,v)\,\tau(t,x)-B(t,x),$$

where

$$E(t,x,v):=L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot v-L(t,x,v)=K(v)+U(t,x)$$

is the **mechanical energy function of the chart**
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]). Since $L_{v}=\mathsf M v$,

$$C(t,x,v)=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-\bigl(K(v)+U(t,x)\bigr)\tau(t,x)-B(t,x).$$

**(d) Dimensions and rescaling.** Read the family parameter $s$ as carrying a
declared unit $\sigma$ (for instance radians for a rotation family, seconds
for a time-reparametrisation family, or a dimensionless parameter). Then
$\tau$ has dimension $\tau\sigma^{-1}$, every component
$\xi_{i}$ has dimension $\ell\sigma^{-1}$, $B$ has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\sigma^{-1}$ (action per parameter unit) and
$C$ has the same dimension as $B$
([[def-cm01-units]]). Replacing $(\tau,\xi,B)$ by $(c\tau,c\xi,cB)$ with
a real constant $c\ne0$ — the same family reparametrised by $s\mapsto cs$ —
rescales $C$ by $c$.

**(e) Status.** This item fixes the model's symmetry vocabulary: which data
satisfy the model's Noether identity, and which function is their charge. It
asserts neither that a given model admits a nonzero symmetry datum, nor that
the charge of a datum is conserved. Conservation is proved under explicit
hypotheses by the theorems of this page, and the hypotheses must be verified
against the declared potential $U$ and the masses: a change of inertial frame,
the affine structure of the spacetime of [[post-cm01-spacetime]], or a
relabelling of the particle labels is a kinematic or descriptive operation and
is not by itself a symmetry datum of $L$. Every statement that uses a charge
names the potential representative used
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c)); the effect of
changing the representative is recorded in the general Noether theorem of this
page.
items.physical_scope: The symmetry vocabulary of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: symmetry data as triples (tau, xi, B) satisfying the model's Noether identity for the mechanical Lagrangian K - U, strict data and their exact relation to the chart-level infinitesimal point symmetries, the charge M v . xi - (K+U) tau - B together with its dimension and its behaviour under rescaling of the family parameter, and the status of the notion. The item defines only; it asserts no conservation law, no existence of any symmetry of a given model, and no empirical content.

items.title: The point Noether theorem of the model: conservation of the charge of a strict symmetry, and the residual-force rate
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let $(\tau,\xi,B)$ be a
symmetry datum of the model's mechanical Lagrangian with $\tau\equiv0$
([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]] clause (a)); write

$$C(t,x,v):=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-B(t,x)\qquad\bigl((t,x,v)\in O\bigr)$$

for its charge. Then:

1. **(conservation in the global potential model).** If $d\equiv0$ and $\xi$
   is independent of $t$, then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an
   interval $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the
   function $t\mapsto C\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$ is constant on $J$.

2. **(residual-force rate).** For an arbitrary presentation $(U,d)$, along
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ the function $t\mapsto C(t,x(t),x'(t))$ is of class
   $C^{1}$ on $J$ and

$$C'(t)=\bigl\langle d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr),\,\xi\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J),$$

   where the pairing is the Euclidean inner product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$;
   consequently $C$ is constant on $J$ if and only if this pairing vanishes
   for every $t\in J$.

Clause 1 is the conditional conservation law of the model's global potential
branch under a symmetry identity of its Lagrangian; clause 2 quantifies the
exact rate at which a residual force destroys it. Neither clause asserts that
any model possesses a strict symmetry datum, and neither carries empirical
content.
items.physical_scope: The point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a strict symmetry datum of the mechanical Lagrangian that is independent of time, the charge M x' . xi - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; for an arbitrary presentation the charge of a strict datum has derivative equal to the residual force paired with the generator, so conservation holds exactly when that pairing vanishes along the motion. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation, the symmetry identity and, in the conservation clause, on the absence of residual forces; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 1.8.5: the Noether integral as the momentum paired with the generator of a parametric coordinate transformation, with the central-force rotation example

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.3, printed pages 12-15 (PDF pages 15-18): cyclic coordinates and the conserved canonical momentum, with the centre-of-mass momentum and rotational angular-momentum examples

items.title: The general Noether theorem of the model: point transformations with time reparametrisation, the charge $p\cdot\xi-E\tau-B$, its residual-force rate and its potential gauge
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let $(\tau,\xi,B)$ be a
symmetry datum of the model's mechanical Lagrangian
([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]] clause (a)), with charge

$$C(t,x,v):=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-\bigl(K(v)+U(t,x)\bigr)\tau(t,x)-B(t,x)\qquad\bigl((t,x,v)\in O\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **(conservation in the global potential model).** If $d\equiv0$, then for
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
   interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto C\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$ is constant on $J$.

2. **(specialisations).** At $\tau\equiv0$ the model identity is the strict
   identity of clause (b) of [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]
   and the charge reduces to $(\mathsf M v)\cdot\xi-B$; at $\xi\equiv0$,
   $\tau\equiv1$, $B\equiv0$ the model identity holds on $O$ if and only if
   $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$, and the charge is $-E$, where
   $E=K+U$ is the model's mechanical energy function.

3. **(residual-force rate).** For an arbitrary presentation $(U,d)$, along
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ the function $t\mapsto C(t,x(t),x'(t))$ is of class
   $C^{1}$ on $J$ and

$$C'(t)=\Bigl\langle d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr),\,\xi\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)-x'(t)\,\tau\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J);$$

   consequently $C$ is constant on $J$ if and only if this pairing vanishes
   for every $t\in J$.

4. **(potential gauge).** Let $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$ and let
   $U':=U+c$ be the representative of
   [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c), with Lagrangian
   $L'=K-U'$; put $B':=B-c\tau$. Then $(\tau,\xi,B')$ is a symmetry datum of
   the model's mechanical Lagrangian for the representative $U'$ if and only
   if $(\tau,\xi,B)$ is one for $U$, and its charge is the same function $C$.
   In particular the conserved quantity of clause 1 does not depend on the
   choice of potential representative, although the mechanical energy
   $E=K+U$ does.

All clauses are conditional deductions from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the stated symmetry identity; no clause asserts that
a given model admits a symmetry datum, and no clause carries empirical content.
items.physical_scope: The general point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a symmetry datum with time reparametrisation, the charge M x' . xi - (K+U) tau - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; the charge has derivative equal to the residual force paired with xi - x' tau for an arbitrary presentation; the tau=0 and xi=0, tau=1 specialisations reduce to the strict point-symmetry charge and to minus the mechanical energy; and replacing the potential representative U by U+c(t) with the boundary function B-c tau preserves the identity and leaves the charge unchanged. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the symmetry identity; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law, no converse from conservation to symmetry, and carries no empirical content.

items.title: Time translation and the mechanical energy of the model: conservation in the autonomous global potential branch and the sharp failure for a time-dependent potential
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let

$$E(t,x,v):=K(v)+U(t,x)=\frac12\,v\cdot\mathsf M v+U(t,x)$$

be the model's mechanical energy function. Consider the datum
$\tau\equiv1$, $\xi\equiv0$, $B\equiv0$ of
[[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]. Then:

For this time-translation family take its parameter $s$ to be measured in
seconds; $\tau\equiv1$ is dimensionless and the charge $-E$ has units of
action per second, namely joules.

1. **(the identity).** The datum satisfies the model's Noether identity on
   $O$ if and only if $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$; its charge is
   the function $-E$.
2. **(conservation).** If $d\equiv0$ and $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$, then for
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
   interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto E\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=K(x'(t))+U(t,x(t))$ is constant on $J$.
3. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$
   with $\partial_{t}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$, then the maximal motion
   $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ of the model through the initial datum
   $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies
   $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(K(x_{\max}')+U(\cdot,x_{\max})\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=\partial_{t}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$,
   and the mechanical energy is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

The conservation clause is the energy case of the model's Noether identity and
is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared representative $U$ and
the absence of residual forces; the sharpness clause shows that explicit time
dependence of the declared representative destroys conservation along an actual
motion. No empirical content is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Time translation as a symmetry datum of the force model with a declared potential presentation: with a time-valued family parameter in seconds, the datum (tau,xi,B)=(1,0,0) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the potential has no explicit time dependence; in the global potential branch with an autonomous potential the mechanical energy K+U is constant along every motion; and in that branch, if the potential depends explicitly on time at a state, then the maximal motion through that state has nonvanishing energy derivative there, so the energy is not conserved. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation; the sharpness clause uses the maximal-motion existence theorem, and no empirical content is asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.4.1 'Homogeneity of Time', printed page 26 (PDF page 32): for a Lagrangian with no explicit time dependence the function H = sum qdot_j p_j - L is constant, identified with the total energy for the systems considered

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 2.3, chapter pages 7-10 (PDF pages 25-28): dH/dt = -dL/dt explicitly, so H is an integral of motion when the Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence, while the mechanical energy need not coincide with H

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.3, printed page 15 (PDF page 18): if H has no explicit time dependence then H is conserved, and energy is conserved when the energy is time independent

items.title: Translation symmetry of the model's Lagrangian and conservation of total momentum: exact hypothesis, conservation and its sharpness
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. For the translation family take
the parameter $s$ to have units of length and let $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ be a
nonzero dimensionless vector. Let $\xi^{a}\in\mathbb R^{3N}$ be the configuration
vector whose $i$-th three-dimensional block is $\xi^{a}_{i}:=a$, so that
$(\mathsf M v)\cdot\xi^{a}=\sum_{i}m_{i}\,a\cdot v_{i}$ for a
velocity $v$. Write $P(t):=\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total momentum of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]. Then:

1. **(infinitesimal and finite invariance).** The following are equivalent:
   (i) $\sum_{i=1}^N a\cdot\nabla_{x_i}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_0\times Q$; (ii) $U(t,x+s\xi^a)=U(t,x)$ whenever
   the whole segment $\{x+r\xi^a:r\text{ between }0\text{ and }s\}$
   lies in $Q$. More generally, for fixed $(t,x)$ put
   $J_x:=\{s\in\mathbb R:x+s\xi^a\in Q\}$, an open set containing $0$.
   Its interval components are its maximal open intervals. Under (i),
   $s\mapsto U(t,x+s\xi^a)$ is constant on each interval component.
   Invariance for every $s\in J_x$, including components separated by an
   excluded segment, holds if and only if all these component constants
   equal $U(t,x)$. This agreement is automatic when $J_x$ is connected,
   in particular when the whole translation line lies in $Q$.

2. **(the symmetry datum).** Under these equivalent hypotheses the strict
   datum $\tau\equiv0$, $\xi\equiv\xi^{a}$, $B\equiv0$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]].

3. **(conservation of the momentum component).** If in addition $d\equiv0$,
   then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with
   nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto a\cdot P(t)=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a,\,m_{i}x_{i}'(t)\bigr\rangle$
   is constant on $J$.

4. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state
   $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$, then the maximal motion
   $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ through the initial datum $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$
   satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(a\cdot P(t)\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=-g\ne0$; in
   particular $a\cdot P$ is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

5. **(vector form).** If $\sum_{i}\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$, then with $d\equiv0$ the total momentum vector
   $P$ is constant along every motion.

The hypotheses are conditions on the declared potential; the conservation
clauses are conditional deductions of the global potential branch, the
sharpness clause locates the failure at an actual motion, and no symmetry of
any particular force law and no empirical content is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Translation symmetry of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: with a dimensionless direction vector and a length-valued translation parameter, the exact equivalence between the differential invariance condition sum_i a . grad_i U = 0 and finite invariance on admissible translation segments, with the exact component compatibility criterion for all admissible endpoints, the resulting strict symmetry datum and conservation of the component a . P of the total momentum along every motion of the global potential branch, the sharpness statement in that branch that a nonzero directional derivative at a state produces a motion whose momentum component is not constant, and the vector form for a fully translation-invariant potential. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no translation symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

items.title: Rotation symmetry of the model's Lagrangian and conservation of angular momentum about the origin
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Take the rotation parameter $s$
to be measured in radians, treated as dimensionless in SI, and take $a$ to be
dimensionless; thus $\lvert a\rvert s$ is dimensionless and the charge
$a\cdot J$ has angular-momentum units (action). Fix a nonzero vector
$a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and put, for $s\in\mathbb R$ and $z\in\mathbb R^{3}$,

$$R_{a}(s)z:=z+\frac{\sin\bigl(\lvert a\rvert s\bigr)}{\lvert a\rvert}\,a\times z+\frac{1-\cos\bigl(\lvert a\rvert s\bigr)}{\lvert a\rvert^{2}}\,a\times(a\times z),$$

where $\times$ is the cross product of $\mathbb R^{3}$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). For a configuration $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$
write $R_{a}(s)x:=(R_{a}(s)x_{1},\dots,R_{a}(s)x_{N})$, and let
$\xi^{a}:Q\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be the vector field with $\xi^{a}_{i}(x):=a\times x_{i}$.
Write $J(t):=\sum_{i}x_{i}(t)\times m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total angular
momentum about the inertial origin ([[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]).
Then:

1. **(infinitesimal and finite invariance).** The following are equivalent:
   (i) $\sum_i\langle a\times x_i,\nabla_{x_i}U(t,x)\rangle=0$
   for every $(t,x)\in I_0\times Q$; (ii) $U(t,R_a(s)x)=U(t,x)$
   whenever $\{R_a(r)x:r\text{ between }0\text{ and }s\}$ lies in $Q$.
   More generally put $D_x:=\{s\in\mathbb R:R_a(s)x\in Q\}$, an open set
   containing $0$, with interval components its maximal open intervals.
   Under (i), $s\mapsto U(t,R_a(s)x)$ is constant on each interval
   component. Invariance for every $s\in D_x$, including components
   separated by an excluded arc, holds if and only if all these constants
   equal $U(t,x)$. This agreement is automatic if $D_x$ is connected,
   in particular if the whole rotation orbit is contained in $Q$.

2. **(the symmetry datum).** Under these equivalent hypotheses the strict
   datum $\tau\equiv0$, $\xi\equiv\xi^{a}$, $B\equiv0$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]].

3. **(conservation of the angular-momentum component).** If in addition
   $d\equiv0$, then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval
   $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto a\cdot J(t)=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a,\,x_{i}(t)\times m_{i}x_{i}'(t)\bigr\rangle$
   is constant on $J$.

4. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state
   $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a\times x_{0,i},\,\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\bigr\rangle\ne0$,
   then the maximal motion $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ through the initial datum
   $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies
   $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(a\cdot J(t)\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=-g\ne0$; in particular
   $a\cdot J$ is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

5. **(vector form).** If $\sum_{i}x_{i}\times\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$, then with $d\equiv0$ the total angular momentum
   vector $J$ is constant along every motion.

The hypothesis is a condition on the declared potential — equivalently, by
clause 1, invariance of $U$ along admissible arcs of the simultaneous rotations
$R_a(s)$ of all labels, with full endpoint invariance requiring the component
agreement specified there; the conservation clauses are conditional deductions of the global
potential branch, and no symmetry of any particular force law and no empirical
content is asserted.

J of the total angular momentum about the inertial origin along every motion of the global potential branch, its sharpness in that branch under a nonzero rotational derivative of U, and the vector form when the potential is invariant under all rotations about the origin. items.title: The Galilean boost charge of the model: exact condition, uniform centre-of-mass motion, the induced motions and the boundary of the conservation law
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. For this boost family take the
parameter $s$ to have units of velocity and take $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ to be
dimensionless; then $st a$ is a displacement, $\xi^{a}=t\mathbf a$ with
$\mathbf a:=(a,\dots,a)\in\mathbb R^{3N}$ has units of time, and $B^{a}$ and
$K_{a}$ have units $\mathrm{kg\,m}$, equal to
action per unit velocity. Fix a nonzero vector
$a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and consider the maps

$$\xi^{a}(t,x):=t\mathbf a,\qquad B^{a}(t,x):=a\cdot\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i},$$

so that $(\tau,\xi,B)\equiv(0,\xi^{a},B^{a})$ is a datum of
[[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]. Write
$P(t):=\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total momentum and $X(t)$ for the
centre of mass of [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], where the scalar
total mass is $M:=\sum_i m_i$ and $M X(t)=\sum_i m_i x_i(t)$; thus
along a motion $B^{a}(t,x(t))=M\,a\cdot X(t)$. Define the **boost charge**

$$K_{a}(t):=a\cdot\bigl(t\,P(t)-M X(t)\bigr)=t\,\bigl(a\cdot P(t)\bigr)-\sum_{i}m_{i}\,a\cdot x_{i}(t).$$

Then:

1. **(the identity).** The datum $(0,\xi^{a},B^{a})$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ if and only if the translation-invariance condition
   $\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for all $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$
   of clause 1 of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] holds.
2. **(conservation).** If in addition $d\equiv0$, then for every motion
   $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty interior
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function $t\mapsto K_{a}(t)$ is constant
   on $J$.
3. **(uniform centre-of-mass motion).** Under the hypotheses of clause 2, the
   function $t\mapsto M\,a\cdot X(t)$ is affine on $J$ with slope
   $a\cdot P$.
4. **(boosted motions).** Under the hypotheses of clause 2, let $x:J\to Q$
   be a motion and $s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $x(t)+st\mathbf a\in Q$ for every
   $t\in J$. Then $\widetilde x(t):=x(t)+st\mathbf a$ is a motion if and only if
   $\nabla_xU(t,\widetilde x(t))=\nabla_xU(t,x(t))$ for every $t\in J$.
   This equality, and hence the boosted-motion conclusion, follows if
   each segment between $x(t)$ and $\widetilde x(t)$ is contained in $Q$,
   or if the all-admissible-endpoint finite invariance criterion of
   [[pthm-cm08-translation]] clause 1 holds.

5. **(the general rate and the boundary).** For an arbitrary presentation
   $(U,d)$ and every motion $x:J\to Q$,

$$K_{a}'(t)=t\,a\cdot F_{\mathrm{tot}}(t),\qquad F_{\mathrm{tot}}(t):=\sum_{i}F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr);$$

   consequently, when $d\equiv0$, the charge $K_{a}$ is constant on $J$ if and
   only if $t\mapsto t\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x(t))$ vanishes
   identically on $J$, and if the translation-invariance condition fails at
   some state, then there are a time $t_{0}\ne0$ and a state $x_{0}$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$ such that the maximal
   motion through $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies $K_{a}'(t_{0})=-t_{0}\,g\ne0$
   and $K_{a}$ is not constant on its interval.

The charge exists as a conserved quantity exactly under the same potential
invariance that conserves the momentum component $a\cdot P$; the conservation
clauses are conditional deductions of the global potential branch, and no
empirical content is asserted.
items.physical_scope: The Galilean boost charge of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: with dimensionless a and a velocity-valued family parameter, the time-dependent symmetry datum (tau, xi, B) = (0, t a, a . M x) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the differential translation condition sum_i a . grad_i U = 0 holds; in the global potential branch the boost charge a . (t P - M X) is then constant, the component a of the centre of mass moves uniformly, and the boosted curves t -> x(t) + s t a of motions are again motions; for an arbitrary presentation the exact rate of the charge is the time times the component a of the total force, while nonconservation from a nonzero translation derivative is asserted in the global potential branch. The charge has dimension mass times length (action per velocity), and its rate has momentum dimensions. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no boost invariance of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

items.title: The energy function of a moving chart: exact difference from the inertial mechanical energy and conservation along the chart solutions
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
be open and nonempty and let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be of class $C^{3}$ with
$X_{q}(t,q)$ invertible for every $(t,q)\in\Omega$; let

$$\widetilde O:=\bigl\{(t,q,v)\in\Omega\times\mathbb R^{3N}:\bigl(t,X(t,q),X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)\in O\bigr\},\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(t,q),\,X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)$$

be the substituted data of [[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]].
Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior, with derivatives at any included
endpoints understood one-sided, and let $q:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
$(t,q(t),q'(t))\in\widetilde O$ for every $t\in J$, and put $x(t):=X(t,q(t))$.
Define the **chart energy function** and the **inertial mechanical energy**
along the curve by

$$e(t):=q'(t)\cdot\widetilde L_{v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)-\widetilde L\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr),\qquad E_{\mathrm{in}}(t):=K\bigl(x'(t)\bigr)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **(difference identity).** For every $t\in J$,

$$E_{\mathrm{in}}(t)=e(t)+\bigl\langle X_{t}\bigl(t,q(t)\bigr),\,\mathsf M x'(t)\bigr\rangle;$$

   equivalently
   $e(t)=\tfrac12\langle X_{q}v,\mathsf M X_{q}v\rangle-\tfrac12\langle X_{t},\mathsf M X_{t}\rangle+U(t,X)$
   at $(t,q(t),q'(t))$.
2. **(coincidence criterion).** $e(t)=E_{\mathrm{in}}(t)$ if and only if
   $\langle X_{t}(t,q(t)),\mathsf M x'(t)\rangle=0$; in particular
   $e=E_{\mathrm{in}}$ along the curve whenever $X_{t}(t,q(t))=0$.
3. **(conservation of the chart energy).** If
   $\widetilde L_{t}(t,q(t),q'(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$ and $q$ solves the
   chart Euler-Lagrange equation $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $J$, then $e$ is
   constant on $J$; this includes in particular the case
   $\widetilde L_{t}\equiv0$ on $\widetilde O$.
4. **(model motions in the global potential branch).** If $d\equiv0$ and
   $x:J\to Q$ is a motion of the model with $q$ its chart description, then
   $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $J$.

The difference identity and the coincidence criterion hold for every
presentation; clauses 3 and 4 are the conservation statement of the moving
description and its link to the model's motions. No identification of the
chart energy function with the inertial mechanical energy is asserted, and no
empirical content is claimed.
items.physical_scope: The energy bookkeeping of a time-dependent coordinate description of the force model: for a C^3 coordinate map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian and the substituted Lagrangian of the covariance theorem, the chart energy function equals the inertial mechanical energy plus or minus the pairing of the chart's explicit time dependence with the mass-operator velocity, so the two agree exactly when that pairing vanishes; the chart energy function is conserved along chart Euler-Lagrange solutions whenever the substituted Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence along the trajectory; and in the global potential branch the chart description of every motion solves that chart equation. The statement concerns the model's coordinate description, is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and asserts no measurement and no identification of the chart energy with the inertial mechanical energy.

Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 2.3, chapter pages 7-10 (PDF pages 25-28): the Hamiltonian function of the bead on the rotating ring differs from the mechanical energy by mR^2 omega^2 sin^2(theta) while H itself is conserved because the Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence

items.title: Scope of the symmetry-conservation statements: force laws that break kinematic symmetries, residual forces, moving coordinates and the empirical boundary
items.statement:
- **Symmetries are properties of the model, not of the kinematics.** The
  symmetry criteria of this page are identities imposed on the model's
  declared mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ and its residual forces
  ([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]); the affine structure
  of spacetime, the availability of every inertial frame and the Galilean
  transformation law do not by themselves make a potential invariant. For the
  uniform-force potential $U=-\sum_i m_i\mathbf g\cdot x_i$ with $d\equiv0$,
  $\sum_i\nabla_{x_i}U=-M_{\mathrm{tot}}\mathbf g$: translations are
  symmetries exactly in dimensionless directions $a\perp\mathbf g$, and a direction with
  $a\cdot\mathbf g\ne0$ gives a momentum and boost charge that fail along
  motions. The sharpness clauses locate that failure along maximal motions
  through states where their required directional derivative is nonzero.

  A mass-weighted confining potential
  $U=\tfrac{k}{2}\sum_i m_i\lvert x_i-x_i^0\rvert^2$, $k>0$, has
  $\sum_i\nabla_{x_i}U=kM(X-X_0)$, where
  $X_0=M^{-1}\sum_i m_i x_i^0$. In the global potential model, for any
  direction with $a\cdot(X-X_0)\ne0$ the translation condition fails and
  the momentum charge is not conserved along the maximal motion through that
  state. If that state's time is nonzero, the boost sharpness clause also
  applies; at time zero, continuity gives nearby nonzero times with the same
  nonvanishing directional derivative. Here $k$ has units $\tau^{-2}$, so
  $U$ has energy units and the centre-of-mass equation is
  $X''=-k(X-X_0)$.

- **Rotation is not translation.** The rotation condition of
  [[pthm-cm08-rotation]] is compatible with a confining central potential: for
  $U$ depending only on the labels through rotation-invariant combinations the
  angular-momentum charge for a dimensionless rotation generator may be
  conserved in the global potential branch even when the translation charges
  are not. The conservation statements are
  separate conditional claims, one per symmetry datum; a model can possess one
  charge and fail another.

- **Residual forces destroy charges at a computable rate.** With
  $d\not\equiv0$ the charge of a strict symmetry is conserved exactly when the
  residual force pairs to zero with the generator along the motion
  ([[pthm-cm08-point-noether]] clause 2), and for a general datum with time
  reparametrisation the rate is the residual force paired with
  $\xi-v\tau$ ([[pthm-cm08-general-noether]] clause 3). A friction force along
  a translation generator, for instance, changes the corresponding momentum
  charge whenever its total pairing with that generator is nonzero along the
  motion. The balance theorems of
  the force page, in particular [[pthm-cm03-energy-balance]], remain valid in
  those situations and carry the residual contribution explicitly; the
  Noether charges and the balance identities are different deductions, and
  neither replaces the other.

- **Moving coordinates and the mechanical energy.** In a time-dependent
  coordinate description the chart energy function of
  [[pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function]] differs from the inertial
  mechanical energy by the pairing of the chart's explicit time dependence
  with the mass-operator velocity, and the chart energy can be conserved while
  that difference is nonzero; the phrase "the Hamiltonian is conserved" is
  therefore not by itself a statement about the inertial mechanical energy.
  Similarly, a potential with $\partial_t U\not\equiv0$ satisfies the
  time-translation identity of [[pthm-cm08-time-energy]], with parameter
  measured in seconds, exactly when its explicit time dependence vanishes, and
  in the global potential branch the
  sharpness clause exhibits a motion through a state where $\partial_t U\ne0$
  whose mechanical energy changes at that rate.

- **No converse and no empirical claim.** The results of this page are
  conditional deductions inside the force model: symmetry hypotheses on the
  declared presentation imply conservation of the stated charges along the
  motions. No converse is asserted — conservation of a quantity along the
  computed motions does not establish that the model has the corresponding
  symmetry datum — and no observational content is introduced. If a
  conservation statement is used in an empirical analysis, the model
  assumptions, the representative of the potential and any measured inputs
  enter that analysis as additional premises with their own qualifications;
  an observation consistent with a conservation law is evidence about the
  combined model and apparatus, not a proof of either.

- **Not asserted.** The page does not treat discrete symmetries, Noether's
  second theorem, field-theoretic charges, gauge families whose generators
  fail to be $C^{2}$, global existence of the transformation families, or the
  question whether any physical interaction is invariant under the families
  considered; those are separate mathematical and empirical developments.
items.physical_scope: Scope audit of the symmetry and conservation statements of the pair: the symmetry criteria are conditions on the declared model Lagrangian and potential, not on the kinematic framework; in the global potential branch (d=0), force laws with external or confining potentials can break the corresponding charges, with the failure rates computed by the sharpness clauses; for arbitrary presentations, residual-force terms can cancel or add to those rates, and the exact rates are supplied by the Noether statements; in a moving coordinate description the conserved chart energy function need not be the inertial mechanical energy; explicit time dependence breaks energy conservation in the global potential branch when it is nonzero at an adopted state; and no converse from an observed conservation to a symmetry of a model, and no empirical claim, is asserted. The remark adds no new physical claim.

items.title: The uniform-force model: translation and boost charges fail across the field while the energy survives, with exact rates and a numerical instance
items.statement:
Work in the one-label uniform-force model of [[ex-cm02-uniform-field]]: the
force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$,
time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and
force map $F(t,x,v)=m\,\mathbf g$ for a declared constant parameter
$\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ of dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$
([[def-cm01-units]]). Adopt the **potential presentation**

$$U(t,x):=-m\,\mathbf g\cdot x\qquad\bigl((t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}\bigr),$$

of class $C^{\infty}$ and dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, so that
$-\nabla_{x}U=m\mathbf g=F$ and the model is a global potential model
$d\equiv0$ in the sense of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]];
declare a nonzero dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and consider the motion.
For the boost family, its parameter $s$ is measured in velocity units, so
$K_{a}$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m}$ and $K_{a}'$ has units
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. For the time-translation datum use a parameter
measured in seconds, so its generator value $\tau\equiv1$ is dimensionless
and its charge $-E$ is measured in joules. Consider the motion

$$x(t):=x_{0}+v_{0}\,t+\tfrac12\,\mathbf g\,t^{2}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$

with $x_{0},v_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, which is the unique maximal motion through
$(0,x_{0},v_{0})$ by [[ex-cm02-uniform-field]]. Verify:

1. the directional derivative of the potential is
   $a\cdot\nabla_{x}U(t,x)=-m\,a\cdot\mathbf g$, so the translation
   condition of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] clause 1 holds exactly when
   $a\cdot\mathbf g=0$;
2. the momentum component is
   $a\cdot P(t)=m\,a\cdot v_{0}+m\,t\,(a\cdot\mathbf g)$, hence constant on
   $\mathbb R$ exactly when $a\cdot\mathbf g=0$, with rate
   $m\,a\cdot\mathbf g$ otherwise;
3. the boost charge is
   $K_{a}(t)=t\,(a\cdot P(t))-m\,a\cdot x(t)=\tfrac12m\,t^{2}(a\cdot\mathbf g)-m\,a\cdot x_{0}$,
   with rate $\frac{d}{dt}K_{a}(t)=t\,m\,(a\cdot\mathbf g)$;
4. the mechanical energy is
   $E(t)=\tfrac12m\lvert x'(t)\rvert^{2}+U(t,x(t))=\tfrac12m\lvert v_{0}\rvert^{2}-m\,\mathbf g\cdot x_{0}$,
   constant on $\mathbb R$, and the potential has no explicit time
   dependence, so the time-translation identity of
   [[pthm-cm08-time-energy]] clause 1 holds;
5. for the numerical instance $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$,
   $\mathbf g=(0,0,-1)\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, $x_{0}=0$,
   $v_{0}=(1,0,0)\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $a=e_{3}$: at $t=2\,\mathrm s$
   one has $P(2)=(1,0,-2)$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $a\cdot P(2)=-2\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $K_{a}(2)=-2\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m$ and
   $K_{a}'(2)=-2\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, while the
   component along $e_{1}$ is constant at $1\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$.

All values are model values of the declared idealization: the constant field is
an adopted approximation of an external influence and no measurement is
reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the framework: the one-label global potential model (d=0) with U = -m g . x, its explicit maximal motion, the failure of the translation and boost charges in directions with a nonzero component along the field, with the exact rates predicted by the sharpness clauses, a numerical instance at an explicit time, and the survival of the mechanical energy because the potential has no explicit time dependence. The boost direction is dimensionless and its family parameter has velocity units, so the boost charge has mass-length units. All values are model values in a declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any field of nature.

items.title: A two-label pair-potential model: translation, rotation, boost and energy charges verified on the model class and on an explicit rigid-rotation motion
items.statement:
Declare a two-label model of the force branch
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=2$, masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, total
mass $M:=m_{1}+m_{2}$ and reduced mass $\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/M$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain
$Q=\{(x_{1},x_{2})\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{2}:x_{1}\ne x_{2}\}$ (open), and let
$\psi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$; its argument is the
squared separation of dimension $\ell^{2}$, and its values have energy
dimension. Adopt the potential

$$U(x_{1},x_{2}):=\psi\bigl(s(x)\bigr),\qquad s(x):=\lvert x_{1}-x_{2}\rvert^{2},$$

of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, so that the model is a global potential
model $d\equiv0$ of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Verify:

For the translation family use a dimensionless direction and a length-valued
parameter; for rotations use a dimensionless generator and a parameter in
radians; for time translations use a parameter in seconds; for boosts use a
dimensionless direction and a velocity-valued parameter. In the explicit
potential below, $c_{0}$ has energy units
$\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}\,s^{-2}}$ and $\kappa$ has units
$\mathrm{kg\,s^{-2}}$ (energy per squared length).

1. **gradients and pair reading.** For every $x\in Q$,

$$\nabla_{x_{1}}U(x)=2\psi'\bigl(s(x)\bigr)\,(x_{1}-x_{2}),\qquad \nabla_{x_{2}}U(x)=-2\psi'\bigl(s(x)\bigr)\,(x_{1}-x_{2});$$

   so the model invokes the external-plus-pair presentation of
   [[post-cm02-interactions]] with $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}=0$ and a single pair
   force $F_{12}=-F_{21}=-2\psi'(s)(x_{1}-x_{2})$ that is antisymmetric and
   central.
2. **translation.** $\sum_{i}\nabla_{x_{i}}U=0$ identically, so the
   differential condition of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] holds for every
   $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$; consequently $P$ and the boost charge
   $a\cdot(tP-M X(t))$ of [[pthm-cm08-boost-boundary]] are constant along
   every motion and the centre of mass moves uniformly.
3. **rotation.** For every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
   $\sum_{i}\langle a\times x_{i},\nabla_{x_{i}}U\rangle=0$ identically, so the
   condition of [[pthm-cm08-rotation]] holds for every axis; consequently the
   total angular momentum $J=\sum_{i}x_{i}\times m_{i}x_{i}'$ is constant
   along every motion.
4. **energy.** $U$ has no explicit time dependence, so the mechanical energy
   $E=K+U$ is constant along every motion by [[pthm-cm08-time-energy]].
5. **explicit rigid-rotation motion (Hooke-type pair).** Specialise to
   $\psi(s)=c_{0}+\kappa s$ with constants $c_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and
   $\kappa>0$, and put $\Omega:=\sqrt{2\kappa/\mu}$, $X_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
   $e(t):=(\cos\Omega t,\sin\Omega t,0)$, $r_{1}:=(\mu/m_{1})\rho$ and
   $r_{2}:=-(\mu/m_{2})\rho$ for a constant $\rho>0$; $X_{0}$ and $\rho$
   have length dimension and $\Omega$ has dimension $\tau^{-1}$. Then
   $x_{i}(t):=X_{0}+r_{i}e(t)$ defines a motion of the model on $\mathbb R$, and
   along it $P\equiv0$, $J=\Omega\mu\rho^{2}e_{3}$ and $E=c_{0}+2\kappa\rho^{2}$ are constant.
6. **numerical instance.** For $m_{1}=m_{2}=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $\kappa=1\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$,
   $\rho=1\,\mathrm m$, $c_{0}=0\,\mathrm{J}$, $X_{0}=0$: $\mu=\tfrac12$, $\Omega=2\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $r_{1}=\tfrac12\,\mathrm m$, $r_{2}=-\tfrac12\,\mathrm m$ and at $t=0$ one
   has $x_{1}=(\tfrac12,0,0)$, $x_{2}=(-\tfrac12,0,0)$,
   $x_{1}'=(0,1,0)$, $x_{2}'=(0,-1,0)$ in the stated units, $P=0$,
   $J=(0,0,1)\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
   $E=2\,\mathrm J$; also $\nabla_{x_{1}}U(0)=2\kappa(x_{1}-x_{2})=(2,0,0)$
   in newtons and $\nabla_{x_{2}}U(0)=(-2,0,0)$.

All values are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is
reported and no property of a physical pair interaction is asserted.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the conservation statements of the pair on a two-label pair-potential model: for a potential depending on the labels through a C^2 function of the squared separation, the pair force is antisymmetric and central; the translation condition of the momentum theorem and the rotation condition of the angular-momentum theorem hold identically for every field direction and axis; the momentum, angular-momentum, boost and energy charges are therefore conserved along every motion of this global potential model; and an explicit rigid-rotation motion for the attractive Hooke-type potential psi(s)=c0+kappa s is verified together with its charges and a numerical instance. Here c0 has energy units and kappa has energy-per-length-squared units. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any physical pair interaction.

items.title: An oscillator observed in a uniformly rotating chart: the conserved chart Hamiltonian is not the inertial mechanical energy
items.statement:
Work in the one-label force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with
$N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and adopt the potential

$$U(x):=\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert x\rvert^{2},\qquad k>0\ \text{with}\ [k]=\mu\tau^{-2},$$

so that $F(t,x,v)=-\nabla U(x)=-kx$ and the model is a global potential model
$d\equiv0$ of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] whose motions
satisfy $mx''=-kx$ ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]). Fix a rotation rate
$\omega\ne0$ of dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and let $\boldsymbol\omega:=\omega e_{3}$.
Define

$$R(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\omega t)&-\sin(\omega t)&0\\\sin(\omega t)&\cos(\omega t)&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

This matrix is the rotation about $e_{3}$ by angle $\omega t$; the identity
$\sin^{2}(\omega t)+\cos^{2}(\omega t)=1$ gives $R(t)\in SO(3)$, and direct
differentiation gives $R'(t)z=\boldsymbol\omega\times R(t)z$
([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]], [[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]],
[[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Consider the time-dependent chart

$$X(t,q):=R(t)q,\qquad \Omega:=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3},$$

which is of class $C^{\infty}$ with $X_{q}(t,q)=R(t)$ invertible, and the
substituted Lagrangian of [[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]]:

$$\widetilde L(t,q,v)=\tfrac{m}{2}\lvert v+\boldsymbol\omega\times q\rvert^{2}-\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert q\rvert^{2}.$$

Verify:

1. **Legendre data and chart Hamiltonian.** $\widetilde L$ is of mechanical
   type with $G=mI_{3}$, $A(q)=m\,\boldsymbol\omega\times q$ and
   $V(q)=\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert q\rvert^{2}-\tfrac{m}{2}\lvert\boldsymbol\omega\times q\rvert^{2}$,
   hence hyperregular with chart momentum $p=m(v+\boldsymbol\omega\times q)$ and
   Hamiltonian

$$H(t,q,p)=\frac{\lvert p\rvert^{2}}{2m}-p\cdot(\boldsymbol\omega\times q)+\frac{k}{2}\lvert q\rvert^{2}.$$

2. **Difference from the inertial mechanical energy.** Along every $C^{2}$
   curve $q:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ on an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior, the
   inertial mechanical energy
   $E_{\mathrm{in}}=\tfrac{m}{2}\lvert x'\rvert^{2}+\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert x\rvert^{2}$
   with $x=X(t,q)$ and the chart energy function
   $e=q'\cdot\widetilde L_{v}-\widetilde L$ satisfy the difference identity of
   [[pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function]] with
   $\langle X_{t},\mathsf M x'\rangle=p\cdot(\boldsymbol\omega\times q)$, i.e.
   $E_{\mathrm{in}}=H+p\cdot(\boldsymbol\omega\times q)$ along solutions.
3. **Explicit circular motion.** If $k=m\omega^{2}$, then
   $x(t):=r\,R(t)e_{1}$ with $r>0$ of dimension $\ell$ is a motion of the model on $\mathbb R$, its
   chart description is the constant curve $q(t)=re_{1}$ with
   $v\equiv0$ and $p\equiv m\,\boldsymbol\omega\times(re_{1})$, and along it
   $H\equiv0$ while $E_{\mathrm{in}}\equiv m\omega^{2}r^{2}$; the substituted
   Lagrangian has $\widetilde L_{t}\equiv0$, so $H$ is a conserved quantity of
   the chart equations that is not the inertial mechanical energy.
4. **Numerical instance.** For $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $\omega=2\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $r=1\,\mathrm m$ and $k=4\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ one has at $t=0$ the
   data $x=(1,0,0)\,\mathrm m$, $x'=(0,2,0)\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $q=(1,0,0)$, $v=0$ and $p=(0,2,0)\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   with $H=0\,\mathrm J$ and $E_{\mathrm{in}}=4\,\mathrm J$.

All values are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is
reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked computation of the moving-chart energy bookkeeping on an explicit model: the one-label isotropic oscillator with potential U = k |x|^2 / 2, observed in a chart rotating uniformly about the third axis; the substituted Lagrangian, its Legendre data and its Hamiltonian are computed, the difference identity between the chart Hamiltonian and the inertial mechanical energy is verified as the pairing of the chart's angular velocity with the momentum, an explicit circular motion with k = m omega^2 is shown to have chart Hamiltonian zero and inertial mechanical energy m omega^2 r^2, and a numerical instance is evaluated. items.title: A one-label model with a time-dependent potential: the time-translation identity fails and the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence
items.statement:
Work in the one-label force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with
$N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window $I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain
$Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be of class $C^{2}$,
of dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$ (newtons), be a prescribed external drive.
Adopt the **time-dependent potential**

$$U(t,x):=\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert x\rvert^{2}-f(t)\cdot x,\qquad k>0\ \text{with}\ [k]=\mu\tau^{-2},$$

of class $C^{2}$ and dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, and check that the
presentation $(U,0)$ of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] has
force map $F(t,x,v)=-kx+f(t)$ of the standing regularity
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii)), so that the model is a
global potential model ($d\equiv0$) with mechanical energy

$$E(t,x,v)=\tfrac{m}{2}\lvert v\rvert^{2}+\tfrac{k}{2}\lvert x\rvert^{2}-f(t)\cdot x.$$

Verify:

For time translations take the family parameter to be measured in seconds;
then the generator value $\tau\equiv1$ is dimensionless and the charge $-E$
has units of joules.

1. **presentation and identity.** $\nabla_{x}U(t,x)=kx-f(t)$, so
   $-\nabla_{x}U=-kx+f(t)=F$; and
   $\partial_{t}U(t,x)=-f'(t)\cdot x$, so the time-translation datum
   $\tau\equiv1,\xi\equiv0,B\equiv0$ satisfies the model identity of
   [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]] if and only if
   $f'\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R$.
2. **energy rate.** Along every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model,

$$E'(t)=\partial_{t}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=-f'(t)\cdot x(t);$$

   in particular the mechanical energy is not conserved along any motion on
   which $t\mapsto f'(t)\cdot x(t)$ does not vanish identically, and if
   $f'(t_{0})\cdot x_{0}\ne0$ then the maximal motion through $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$
   has nonzero energy derivative at $t_{0}$.
3. **explicit sinusoidally driven motion.** Specialise to
   $f(t):=f_{0}\cos(\Omega t)\,\hat e$ with $f_{0}>0$ of force dimension,
   $\Omega>0$ of dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and a dimensionless unit vector
   $\hat e\in\mathbb R^{3}$, and assume $k\ne m\Omega^{2}$. Then

$$x_{p}(t):=\frac{f_{0}\cos(\Omega t)}{k-m\Omega^{2}}\,\hat e\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$

   is a motion of the model on $\mathbb R$, and along it

$$E(t)=\frac{f_{0}^{2}\bigl[m\Omega^{2}-(k-m\Omega^{2})\cos^{2}(\Omega t)\bigr]}{2(k-m\Omega^{2})^{2}},\qquad E'(t)=\frac{f_{0}^{2}\Omega\,\sin(\Omega t)\cos(\Omega t)}{k-m\Omega^{2}};$$

   at $t_{0}=\pi/(4\Omega)$ one has $E'(t_{0})=f_{0}^{2}\Omega/(2(k-m\Omega^{2}))\ne0$.
4. **numerical instance.** For $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $k=1\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$,
   $\Omega=1/2\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $f_{0}=1\,\mathrm N$ and $\hat e=e_{1}$ one has
   $k-m\Omega^{2}=3/4$ and $x_{p}(t)=\tfrac43\cos(t/2)e_{1}$; at $t=\pi/2\,\mathrm s$
   the values are $x_{p}=\tfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}\,\mathrm m$,
   $x_{p}'=-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{3}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
   $E=-\tfrac19\,\mathrm J$ and $E'=\tfrac13\,\mathrm J\,\mathrm s^{-1}$.

All values are model values of the declared idealization; the drive is adopted
external data and no measurement is reported.
